values.note: Free until 2025; from 2026 $17 a night, taxes included. Paid online on the arrival day before occupying a site, or at a state park ranger station; no self-pay envelopes on site.

fees.source: https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-forests/fees-reservations.html ('Starting in 2026, all forest campgrounds that previously did not charge a camping fee will charge $17 per night'; affected campgrounds: 'Grand Portage State Forest ... McFarland'; 'Fees include taxes.'; 'DNR does not accept self-payment envelopes on site or mail-in payments.') + DNR cmp00057 ('fee': 1), read 2026-11-11

note: Primitive DNR state forest campground at the McFarland Lake landing, about 17 mi up the Arrowhead Trail from Hovland, with a boat ramp, dock and swimming, and access to the Boundary Waters and the Border Route Trail. No trash service (pack it out). --Claude
summary: DNR re-read: 6 sites (stored 5), vault toilet, no garbage service, boat ramp and dock; McFarland is on DNR's list of formerly free forest campgrounds that charge $17 (tax included) from 2026, paid online the same day. Stored $0 fee was out of date. Manager Judge C.R. Magney State Park 218-387-6300. Not waterfront kept (sites not resolvable under canopy). Website to hyphen form.
flags: FEES $0 -> $17: DNR 'Starting in 2026, all forest campgrounds that previously did not charge a camping fee will charge $17 per night' lists 'Grand Portage State Forest ... McFarland'. The stored $0 was the pre-2026 rate.
PHONE: none stored; manager 'Judge C.R. Magney State Park' 218-387-6300 (DNR facility record cmp00057).

WATERFRONT not waterfront kept: on Esri imagery the only openings are the gravel lot north of the road (DNR point 48.054432,-90.055901) and the boat-launch road and ramp to the south-west (ramp about 48.0533,-90.0577); no campsite clearings can be told apart under the canopy, and the DNR gives no site map. Nothing to support a water value; default stays down.
Pin 48.0540,-90.0552 is ~70 m SE of the DNR facility point, in trees between the road and the launch road. No move (sites not locatable).

FIT: no DNR page states site sizes; the old note's 'each site fits a camper/RV' had no source and is dropped. Access is the Arrowhead Trail (county road); DNR posts no road warning. A reviewer may want a caveat that pad size is unconfirmed.
